n: Correspondent Banking and Joint Ventures in Proliferation Financing
ds: Proliferation-linked entities may reach the international financial system via correspondent relationships, nested accounts or joint ventures that mask the involvement of restricted parties. Respondent due diligence and payment-message review are the main tools for detecting this exposure.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
Wolfsberg Group, Correspondent Banking Due Diligence Questionnaire (CBDDQ)
FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services (2016)

rat: Respondent banks, nested accounts and SWIFT message review.

ind.n: Respondent bank with presence or business in jurisdictions of proliferation concern
ind.cx: Respondent holds accounts or branches in higher-risk countries without strong controls.
ind.fp: Global banks operate in many markets.
ind.ds: Respondent holds accounts or branches in higher-risk countries without strong controls.

ind.n: Payments that include references to designated or restricted entities
ind.cx: Payment messages show names, addresses or vessels linked to restricted lists.
ind.fp: Partial name matches generate false hits.
ind.ds: Payment messages show names, addresses or vessels linked to restricted lists.

ind.n: Nested relationships with unidentified downstream banks
ind.cx: Respondent processes payments for other banks without disclosure.
ind.fp: Some nested arrangements are legitimate and permitted.
ind.ds: Respondent processes payments for other banks without disclosure.

ind.n: Joint venture with opaque ownership involving state-affiliated partner in higher-risk country
ind.cx: Joint venture entity has partners or beneficial owners that cannot be verified.
ind.fp: State partners are common in JV structures.
ind.ds: Ownership or governance is opaque and no natural person who owns or controls the entity can be identified after reasonable effort.
ind.cn: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified

ind.n: Payments with missing, truncated or inconsistent ordering or beneficiary information
ind.cx: Messages omit key details or show inconsistent data.
ind.ds: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
ind.cn: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information

ind.n: Trade-related payments through correspondent for goods of proliferation concern
ind.cx: Payments relate to goods on control lists or to parties on alerts.
ind.fp: Generic words can create false hits.
ind.ds: Payments relate to goods on control lists or to parties on alerts.

ind.n: Sudden increase in volume through a respondent or dormant account reactivation
ind.cx: Significant, unexplained increase in activity from a respondent.
ind.ds: Transaction volume or value rises abruptly well beyond historical levels, including through a respondent or reactivated account.
ind.cn: Sudden large increase in transaction volume

ind.n: Respondent processing for front companies of concern in prior reports
ind.cx: Respondent's customers appear in prior internal or external reports.
ind.ds: Respondent's customers appear in prior internal or external reports.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

ctl.n: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
ctl.ds: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.

ctl.n: Periodic respondent review and volume monitoring
ctl.ds: Reviews respondent activity against expected volumes, updates expected activity and restricts routing via higher-risk banks. It keeps correspondent risk assessments current after onboarding.

ctl.n: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.

Screens payment instructions, references and narrative fields for restricted parties, goods, places and concealment language using tuned matching logic. It catches exposure that does not appear in the customer record.
Requires respondents to disclose and approve downstream institutions and detects payment patterns that imply undeclared nested use. It limits exposure to unknown third-tier clients.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

ctl.n: Payment message completeness and quality controls
ctl.ds: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

Sends requests for information to respondents or senders with deadlines, tracking of response quality and escalation of repeated deficiencies. It resolves unexplained activity and pressures partners to improve.

Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.

Contacts the customer, or the relationship manager does so, to obtain and record an explanation of unusual transactions, relationships or recipients, and to test it against evidence. The answer informs whether activity is legitimate or should be escalated.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.
Checks parties against previously filed internal reports, links to reported accounts and feeds report outcomes back into tuning. It spots repeat subjects and sharpens detection.
